items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I accepted. And so I played with him for a long time after that, you know.

ctx.x: There were a couple of other real old time trumpet players we wanted to ask about. One is Clem, Edward Clem.
Edward Clem, yeah, that I played with him. Now that's a country band. He had more work, more country job than a band in here. He was, he could see that Southern Pacific and TP.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: And after Bob Lyons and Edward Clem had a falling out, Edward put me on the bass.

ctx.x: So you started on this guitar playing?
And after Bob Lyons and Edward Clem had a falling out, Edward put me on the bass.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: Edwark Clem, well, that's the one I was talking about on the trumpet, Edwark Clem.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Well, that was the town, that was, uh, that was Ragtime band. Yeah. That was Ragtime band. They had the Frank's, ah, alright. I think that was a good one. That's when Frank takes the band, and he left John Pendleton, well, John Pendleton, you know, he could play a kind of style of music. No. Well, I had another fella. His name was Ned. Yeah. Yeah. That's Terry's band, but men like to travel around, so he went away. See, Frank's taken up on Edwark Clem.

Edwark Clem, well, that's the one I was talking about on the trumpet, Edwark Clem. Oh, yeah. He was another fella that had one eye, too. He used to wear black glasses all the time. You couldn't tell it. My glasses are such an app. Yeah. But he was a good trumpet player, though. Oh, yeah.
